harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured `datauser` with `/srv/data` and a persistent ext3 filesystem quota of 100 MiB (102,400 KiB). Enforcement and reboot persistence were verified without changing Ubuntu 7.10 or kernel 2.6.22-14-generic.
actions_performed: Installed the legacy-compatible Ubuntu Gutsy quota package.
Enabled persistent `usrquota` support on the ext3 root filesystem.
Set matching soft and hard limits of 102,400 KiB.
Confirmed oversized writes fail with `Disk quota exceeded`.
Restarted node1 once and verified recovery, persistent data, active quotas, and enforcement.

evidence.summary: datauser is UID/GID 1001, uses /srv/data as its home, and owns the directory.
ext3 reports 102,400 KiB soft and hard limits; oversized writes failed with Disk quota exceeded both before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Persistent quota configuration on the legacy platform
evidence.summary: The ext3 root mount has persistent usrquota configuration; Ubuntu 7.10, kernel 2.6.22-14-generic, and quota 3.14-8 remain in use.
Captured boot ID d58ab693-a842-4eae-aa03-91294439f54f, active user quota, exact limits, mounted filesystem, and persistent-data checksum.
node1 acknowledged the scheduled native reboot before disconnecting.
After restart, boot ID changed to 54d2cfac-a952-4c0c-83b1-bfe749179917.

evidence.requirement: node1 recovered services, data, and quota state
evidence.summary: The ext3 filesystem remounted with usrquota, quota limits remained active, persistent data retained its checksum, post-restart enforcement succeeded, and SSH recovered and listened on port 22.
